questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was crucial that it was possible to take courses with subject matters that fit my academic interrests and could provide a new prospective. However, it was also important that it was a place where I wanted to explore the culture more.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was possible to find all the necessary information and the University even sent out a handbook with information, which was very helpful. However, it could have been useful to receive this handbook earlier than we did.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: On the first day the host University held an informative orientation. However, most of this information I already had upon arrival. Furthermore, a student organisation held an orientation and had made a forum where all exchange student could talk with each other. This was helpfull for the more practical stuff if people needed help with that. The host university's mobility office was also very quick in their reply.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was not possible in my case. I requested it, but they told me that all the spots where full.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I would recommend living close to the University as most student live here and it is nice not to be depend on the public transport in Rome.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The room I got was though a private partner of the University, however it was not the best. We had trouble with heating and warm water in the winter, which is quite problematic. At the same time I payed more in rent than most of the other students in the area. Therefore, I would recommend to look for housing on your own especially as there is plenty of student houses in the area.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to apply for the University quite early on, where you had to fill out your basic information. When it came closer I had to apply for the courses I wish to have.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The host University sent out a handbook with useful information.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I applied for. However, it was quite a pulse to make a good schedule with 5 courses as a lot of student have less courses and there where a lot of overlaps.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: To look at the website and wait/ask for the handbook and ask the mobility office if necessary as they are quick to reply and super helpful.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I would personally say that I found the academic level lower at the host University than my home University.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very different as UCCPH is interactive and depend on group work, whereas the classes at LUISS primarily was a lecture from the professor. In two of my courses we had to do a presentation in class and got feedback on this, but other than that is was not rather interactive. Ofcourse you were welcome to ask a question and they would also from time to time ask one, but I would say that if you prefer a lot of interaction and group work I would reconsider whether LUISS is the right choice. Personally I liked the style of teaching as you would get the materials explained in class and got an in depth feedback on the work you did, which sometimes can lack at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
European Business Law
Public Comparative Law
European Criminal Law
Eu Substantive Law: Internal Market And Beyond
The Protection Of Human Rights In Europe

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I really liked The Protection Of Human Rights In Europe as the professor was very passionate and critical about the subject. He had a different focus than most professorss I have met at UCPCH regarding human rights in Europe, which of course where interesting to hear. Furthermore, both the professor and the teacher assistent gave an in depth response on a mandatory presentation, even though it was not part of the exam. The same was the case for the exam paper. I like that they spend time on proper feedback. 
A lot of the students also liked European Business Law.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: It was sometimes difficult to get home at night if we where in the other part of the city as the metro is closed at night and the busses can be very unreliable. Luckily I lived close to most of my friends so we could share a taxi or an Uber.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
I would say that if you go to the right places you can find good food and drinks quite cheap, however at least me and my friends also ate out a lot more than at home so end the send it was not less expensive. 
As I wrote above I was surprised how often you needed a taxi to get home if you where far away and it was not possible to walk. Some people bought a subsection to the scooters, so if you like to use these this might be an option for you.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The host institution had an ESN office, which was really to at providing social events in the beginning especially where exchange students could meet each other. They also created a group chat, which in the being was used a lot to meet new people.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
To participate in the events by ESN in the beginning and also ERA makes a lot of fun events though out the semester. Especially the intro week by ESN and maybe one of the trips they do. 
I would say that it is important to go to the events in the beginning as this is where everyone meets and are the most open. Hereafter of course you still meet and fall into talk with new people, but it is defiantly useful to meet some nice people you like at these events in the beginning.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would recommend to take a small trip with your new friends to another city and see the country and to go out and enjoy the nice italian cuisine.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
I found it quite easy. The local people where nice, but it was useful/necessary to learn a couple of everyday frases in italian. 
It actually became more difficult in the end when the turist season came, as they then started seeing me as a tourist (I am blonde) and was not as friendly.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I spend most of the time with other exchange students. I think there is a language barrier, so if you truly wanna socialize with the italian students I would recommend learning italian. I met some in class and at parties, but it was difficult to keep up as there often was a language barrier.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
If you are a blond girl it can be a bit annoying that they will comment on your looks and view men and women a bit different at times. 
They are also a lot more opinionated about what food you order and how much you eat. If you go out and not finish your plate the waiter will comment on it. Another example is when you order coffee and what kind. Theses things they have strong rules about. 
Time is more loose. It will happen that the classes do not start on time and that the bus will be late (if it comes at all). So be patient and do not stress about a little delay.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I appreciated the good food, coffee and wine.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Learn a bit of italian beforehand
2) Join the ESN events 
3) Be aware that the exams is different than at UCPH and can be based partly on something you have to do in class like a presentation or that there can be a difference on the type of exam you can take depending on how much you have participated at classes.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
As stated earlier, it is important to not stress to much about the time as the classes sometimes starts later and sometimes end later that scheduled. It can happen that they go 15-30 minutes over time or start that much later. 
If you have classes close to each other you will just have to list out quietly if it continues for too long (more than 10 minutes).

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To meet people from around the world and to get a new prospective on my academic interrests and on life in general.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: There was noting that could not be fixed, but maybe COVID-19.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
